lessons.title: Rooms

lessons.title: There is a door
lessons.canDo: Say what is in a place
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Leo count the doors and windows in the hallway and kitchen.

items.example: There is a big kitchen.
items.note: Say ‘There is’ when you talk about one thing in a place.

items.example: There are two bedrooms.
items.note: Say ‘There are’ when you talk about two or more things in a place.

items.example: There is a door in the kitchen.
items.note: Use ‘door’ for what you open to go into a room; say ‘doors’ for more than one.

image.describe: a wooden indoor door with a round brass handle

items.example: There are two windows in the living room.
items.note: Use ‘window’ for the glass opening in a wall; say ‘windows’ for more than one.

image.describe: a bright glass window with curtains letting in sunlight

grammar.title: There is / There are
grammar.explanation: Use ‘There is’ for one thing (a door, one window). Use ‘There are’ for two or more things (two doors, three windows).

practice.prompt: Look at the picture. What do you open to go into a room?
practice.explanation: You open a door to go into a room.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of glass letting in sunlight. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: A window lets light into a room.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: There is one door in the bathroom.
practice.answer: There is one door in the bathroom.
options: There is one door in the bathroom.
There are two doors in the bathroom.
There is one window in the bathroom.
practice.explanation: One door uses ‘There is’.

practice.prompt: There is only one window. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use ‘There is’ for one thing: a window.

practice.prompt: There are three windows. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: ___ three windows in the living room.
practice.explanation: Use ‘There are’ for two or more things: three windows.

practice.prompt: Match the beginning with the right ending.
practice.explanation: ‘There is’ goes with one thing; ‘There are’ goes with two or more.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about two doors.
practice.answer: There are two doors in the kitchen.
practice.explanation: Two doors is plural, so use ‘There are’.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: There are two windows in my room.
practice.answer: There are two windows in my room.
practice.explanation: Use ‘There are’ when you count two windows.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: In the living room, there are three windows!

questions.prompt: How many windows are in the kitchen?

lessons.title: Where is it?

items.example: The apple is in the box.
items.note: Say ‘in’ when something is inside a room, cup, or box.

items.example: The book is on the table.
items.note: Say ‘on’ when something rests on top of a table, bed, or chair.

items.example: The cat is under the chair.
items.note: Say ‘under’ when something is below a table, bed, or chair.

items.example: The lamp is next to the sofa.
items.note: Say ‘next to’ when something is right beside another thing.

items.example: There is a small box under the table.
items.note: Use ‘box’ for a container with four sides; say ‘boxes’ for more than one.

image.describe: an open cardboard box sitting on a wooden floor

grammar.title: in, on, under, next to
grammar.explanation: Use these words to say where something is: ‘in’ (inside), ‘on’ (on top), ‘under’ (below), and ‘next to’ (beside).
examples: The cup is on the table.
The box is under the bed.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a container with four sides. Which word fits?

practice.prompt: The apple is inside the box. Complete the sentence.

practice.explanation: Use ‘on’ when something rests on top of a table.

The cat is on the chair.

practice.explanation: ‘Under’ means below the chair.

lessons.title: This and that

items.example: This key is small.
items.note: Use ‘this’ when you point to one thing near you.

items.example: That door is big.
items.note: Use ‘that’ when you point to one thing far from you.

items.example: These keys are on the table.
items.note: Use ‘these’ when you point to two or more things near you.

items.example: Those windows are big.
items.note: Use ‘those’ when you point to two or more things far from you.

items.example: My key is on the table.
items.note: Use ‘key’ for what opens a door; say ‘keys’ for more than one.

image.describe: a shiny metal house key on a simple ring

grammar.title: this, that, these, those
grammar.explanation: Use ‘this’ (one) and ‘these’ (two or more) for things near you. Use ‘that’ (one) and ‘those’ (two or more) for things far from you.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture. What opens a door?
practice.explanation: You use a key to open a door.

practice.prompt: The key is in your hand (near you). Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use ‘This’ for one thing near you.

practice.prompt: The door is far across the room. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use ‘That’ for one thing far from you.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: These keys are on the table.
practice.answer: These keys are on the table.
options: These keys are on the table.
This key is on the table.
Those boxes are on the table.
practice.explanation: ‘These keys’ is for two or more keys near you.

practice.prompt: Match each word with how it is used.
practice.explanation: This/these = near; that/those = far.

practice.prompt: Point to the windows far from you. Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Two or more windows far away use ‘Those’ and ‘are’.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: Use ‘These are’ for plural keys near you.

items.example: Your living room is beautiful!
items.note: Say ‘beautiful’ when a room or place looks really lovely.

image.describe: a sunlit, cozy living room with flowers by a bright window

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a sparkling table and plate. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: Clean means neat with no mess.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a plate and cup with spots. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: Dirty means covered in spots or mess.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: The living room is new and beautiful.
practice.answer: The living room is new and beautiful.
options: The living room is new and beautiful.
The kitchen is small and dirty.
The bedroom is old and cold.
practice.explanation: Listen for ‘new and beautiful’.

practice.prompt: Match the opposite words.
practice.explanation: Clean is the opposite of dirty, and new is the opposite of old.

practice.prompt: The sofa is not old. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use ‘new’ for something that is not old.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence describing the bedroom.
practice.answer: My bedroom is clean and beautiful.
practice.explanation: ‘Clean and beautiful’ describes a lovely, tidy bedroom.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: Use ‘is clean’ to say the kitchen is tidy.

story.hook: Which room has a dirty cup?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat and Mia admire a sparkling clean, beautiful living room with a new sofa, then spot a dirty cup in the kitchen.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Smarty, your living room is beautiful!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Thank you, Mia! That sofa is new, and the room is clean.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: And your bedroom is clean too!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Yes, but look in the kitchen.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Oh! There is a dirty plate and a dirty cup on the table!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Breakfast was delicious, so the kitchen is dirty!

questions.explanation: Smarty says: That sofa is new.
Mia says it is beautiful, and Smarty says it is clean.

questions.prompt: What is dirty in the kitchen?
questions.explanation: Mia says: There is a dirty plate and a dirty cup on the table!

mission.setup: Smarty asks you to describe rooms and things.

turns.smarty: My living room is clean. Is your bedroom clean or dirty?
turns.hint: Say ‘My bedroom is clean’ or ‘My bedroom is dirty’.

turns.smarty: Do you have a new phone or a new computer?
turns.hint: Say ‘I have a new phone’, ‘I have a new computer’, or ‘No’.

turns.smarty: Describe your living room!
turns.example: My living room is clean and beautiful.
turns.hint: Use words like ‘clean’, ‘beautiful’, ‘new’, ‘big’, or ‘small’.

lessons.title: Welcome home
lessons.scenario: Smarty visits Sam’s home and asks questions in the hallway.

items.example: My home is small and clean.
items.note: Use ‘home’ for the place where you live with your family.

image.describe: a warm, welcoming cat family house with a red door and glowing windows

items.example: Is there a TV in your bedroom?
items.note: Start a question with ‘Is there’ when you ask about one thing.

items.example: Are there two bathrooms in your home?
items.note: Start a question with ‘Are there’ when you ask about two or more things.

grammar.title: Is there…? / Are there…?
grammar.explanation: Swap the words to ask a question: ‘Is there a sofa?’ (one thing) and ‘Are there two chairs?’ (two or more things).
examples: Is there a lamp in the living room?
Are there three bedrooms in your home?

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of the place where a family lives. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: Home is the place where you live with your family.

practice.prompt: Ask a question about one sofa. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: ___ a sofa in your living room?
practice.explanation: Use ‘Is there’ to ask about one thing: a sofa.

practice.prompt: Ask a question about two bedrooms. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use ‘Are there’ to ask about two or more things: two bedrooms.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: Is there a computer on the table?
practice.answer: Is there a computer on the table?
options: Is there a computer on the table?
Are there two phones in the box?
There is a lamp next to the bed.
practice.explanation: Listen for ‘Is there a computer on the table?’

practice.prompt: Match each question with the right answer.
practice.explanation: Answer ‘Is there…?’ with ‘Yes, there is’ and ‘Are there…?’ with ‘Yes, there are’.

practice.prompt: Build the question about windows in your home.
practice.answer: Are there big windows in your home?
practice.explanation: Plural ‘windows’ needs ‘Are there’.

practice.prompt: The box is below the chair. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use ‘under’ for below the chair.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: My home is clean and beautiful.
practice.answer: My home is clean and beautiful.
practice.explanation: Use ‘clean and beautiful’ to describe your home.

story.hook: How many bedrooms are in Sam’s home?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat stands inside Sam’s cozy front hallway as Sam gestures proudly toward the clean living room and kitchen.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Hello, Smarty! This is my home!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Your home is beautiful and clean, Sam!

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Thank you! This is our living room. There is a new sofa and a lamp.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Are there two bedrooms in your home?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Yes, there are! One bedroom is for my parents, and this is my bedroom.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Is there a computer on your table?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Yes, there is! My computer and my notebook are on that table.

questions.explanation: Smarty says: Your home is beautiful and clean, Sam!

questions.prompt: How many bedrooms are in Sam’s home?
questions.explanation: Smarty asks ‘Are there two bedrooms…?’ and Sam says ‘Yes, there are!’
Sam says: My computer and my notebook are on that table.

mission.setup: Show Smarty your home and answer his questions in your own words.

turns.smarty: Is there a kitchen in your home?
turns.hint: Say ‘Yes, there is’.

turns.smarty: Are there two or three bedrooms in your home?
turns.hint: Say ‘There are two bedrooms’ or ‘Yes, there are’.

turns.smarty: Describe your home in one sentence!
turns.example: My home is clean and beautiful.
turns.hint: Say ‘My home is clean and beautiful’ or ‘My home is big’.

episode.title: The Small Key in the Box

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Good afternoon, Mia! Good afternoon, Sam! My home is clean today.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat greets Mia and Sam in a sunny hallway.

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: Your living room is beautiful, Smarty! Look at that new lamp next to the sofa.

panels.speaker: Sam
panels.text: Smarty, what is that under the table?

image.describe: Sam points at an old wooden box tucked under a hallway table.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: It is a small box! It is old and dirty.

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: Is there a key for this box?

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Yes! There is a small key on my bedroom table, next to my notebook.

image.describe: Smarty holds a tiny shiny key next to a notebook and pencil on a bedroom table.

panels.speaker: Sam
panels.text: Look! In the box, there is a red apple and a big notebook!

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Whose notebook is this? Who is it for? See you later!

image.describe: Smarty, Mia, and Sam look surprised at a mysterious thick notebook inside the open box.

questions.explanation: Sam asks: What is that under the table?
Smarty says: There is a small key on my bedroom table.

questions.answer: a red apple and a big notebook
options: a red apple and a big notebook
questions.explanation: Sam says: In the box, there is a red apple and a big notebook!
